messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Perf cliff detected in continuous-batching pool rtx-prod-3 — 5xx spike and token latency increase above SLA. Paging on-call.

alicia: got the page, looking now. any obvious recent deploys? :thinking_face:

raj: no deploys in the last hour from release pipeline. metrics show burst in inflight queue length around 3012345600.

marta: KV cache miss rate jumped from 3% -> 58% on shard group g-12, looks like mass eviction. TTLs also shortened across the cluster.

samir: that eviction correlates with a microbatch size regression — some clients started sending high-concurrency short prompts, causing continuous batching to create many tiny microbatches -> KV churn.

alicia: impact? which customers? any errors for embeddings or chat endpoints?

raj: 3 customers hitting elevated tail latency, one (AcmeSearch) saw increased 504s on their /v1/generate route. Overall token throughput down ~28%.

marta: stack traces show KV write amplification during batch merge path, and the async compactor task can't keep up. We're seeing paging to disk on a few nodes.

samir: reproducer: run a synthetic workload with 400 concurrent short-seq requests (seq len < 20) and microbatch target 4; you'll see batching jitter and frequent cache evictions.

alicia: ok immediate mitigation plan: 1) throttle concurrent client burst at edge for low-token requests 2) temporarily increase microbatch target  to reduce number of microbatches 3) disable aggressive prefix caching to avoid thrash 4) alert SRE to scale KV workers.

alicia: @raj can you push the edge throttle rule to limit short prompts to 200 rps per customer? simple rate-limit patch.

raj: pushing rule now. command:
```
# edge config snippet
routes:/v1/generate: {
  short_prompt_policy: { max_rps_per_key: 200, token_threshold: 32 }
}
```

raj: rolled. new rules active at 3012345755. monitoring.

marta: I'm bumping microbatch target from 4 -> 12 on the affected pool to consolidate requests. applying hotpatch to cont-batch config, will do canary on 10% of nodes.

samir: note — increasing microbatch size may increase latency for single-request tails, but should improve throughput and reduce KV churn. that's acceptable for now.

marta: hotpatch applied to canary nodes at 3012345782. canary looks stable: queue length flattened, eviction rate down to 9% on canary.

alicia: escalate to scale KV workers by +20% to give compactor time. @ops-bot start scale action.

ops-bot: scaling kv-workers group g-12 by 20% — started at 3012345795. ETA ~2m.

incident-bot: customer-impact update: AcmeSearch seeing 504s reduced from 15% -> 4% since edge throttle + canary microbatch patch. Continue monitoring.

raj: after full rollout of microbatch target and edge throttle (starting at 3012345808), global eviction rate down to 7%, tail latency improving. still watching for jitter.

marta: follow-up: we'll add a short-term change to caching policy to fall back to read-through for hot prefixes instead of aggressive invalidation. draft config:
```
{"kv_policy":"read-through-fallback","hot_prefix_threshold":0.7}
```
Apply after final rollout.

alicia: handing off to night on-call. Summary for next shift: root cause = burst of tiny high-concurrency requests causing microbatch fragmentation and KV cache thrash -> mass evictions -> paging and perf cliff. Mitigations applied: edge short-prompt throttle, increased microbatch target (canary -> full), scaled KV workers + cache policy fallback. Customer impact reduced but not fully back to baseline. Next steps: run load tests for varied seq distributions, add adaptive microbatching heuristic (by seq len), and retain extra KV capacity for 12h.

alicia: tagging on-call: @samir you own the postmortem, include reproducer and perf numbers. ping if anything regresses. :thumbsup:

samir: will do, starting draft now. adding timelines and metrics capture.

ops-bot: incident closed to active mitigation at 3012345890. will watch for 2h quiet period and then debrief.
